note: Ranked improvement backlog for the PSX Trade Desk. Written weekly by the psx-desk-product-scout task (proposes + ranks only, never builds). The owner picks items to implement. score = impact(high3/med2/low1) / effort(high3/med2/low1); higher = do sooner.

items.title: High-severity price-series glitches can reach ticker charts without a visible warning
items.why: state/verify.json built 2026-09-12 flags LSEVL, MDTL, CLCPS and USVIX with high-severity price_series issues and says recent stats may be wrong. pageTicker fetches verify.json, but only consumes room.price_staleness, fundamentals.div_yield and claim.price; the chart and derived stats still render from history/history_deep without showing the price-series warning. This is the remaining high-severity issue type after the broader verify-json-unsurfaced-qa item was marked done.
items.existing_check: Read dashboard/app.js:3014-3017 and 3051: pageTicker selects only three issue fields and then chooses history_deep/history for series; no price_series consumer exists. Confirmed all four high-severity entries and their backend-authored messages in state/verify.json.
items.change: Render the backend-authored price_series issue in the ticker QA area and associate it with the chart/stat section.
items.user_benefit: Readers can tell when a chart or derived metric may be unreliable before treating it as evidence.
items.scope_dependencies: dashboard/app.js consumer only; depends on existing state/verify.json and its current producer.
items.build_scope: Dashboard ticker QA consumer; reuse existing state/verify.json price_series messages and do not change the verifier producer.
items.recommended_first_stage: Wire the existing high-severity message into the ticker warning card for the four currently flagged symbols.
items.tradeoffs: Adds warning friction to four ticker pages, but keeps the intervention limited to high-severity evidence risk.
items.acceptance_test: Each high-severity price_series ticker shows the verify.json message before or beside chart/stat output; clean tickers are unchanged and no warning logic is re-derived in JavaScript.

items.title: Compact Desk Room reveal calls every flagged QA session simply 'QA checked'
items.why: The compact reveal badge in pageTicker is green whenever s.qa exists, regardless of verdict. Current QA notes for FFC, MCB, HBL and HUBC are flagged and include unresolved or material caveats, but those notes appear only after opening the full transcript. A skimming reader can therefore read 'QA checked' as clean verification when the stored verdict is flagged. This is distinct from the already-resolved missing-badge and reaffirmation-freshness items.
items.existing_check: Read dashboard/app.js:4043: s.qa truthiness maps directly to qabadge ok 'QA checked'; compare current state/rooms.json QA notes for FFC, MCB, HBL and HUBC, all with flagged/flags verdicts and substantive caveats.
items.change: Map QA verdicts to distinct compact badges and show a short caveat when the verdict is flagged.
items.user_benefit: A quick scan communicates the difference between clean verification and verification with material caveats.
items.scope_dependencies: dashboard/app.js and existing qabadge styles; no new data source required.
items.build_scope: Dashboard Desk Room reveal header and existing qabadge styles; use room.qa.verdict and room.qa.note only.
items.recommended_first_stage: Handle clean, flagged/flags and not-yet-verified in the reveal header, with the existing QA note as the caveat source.
items.tradeoffs: A less reassuring badge may slow scanning, but it prevents a flagged review from reading like a clean pass.
items.acceptance_test: Compact reveal distinguishes clean, flagged and not-yet-verified states and exposes a concise flagged caveat; blocked sessions remain withheld and the full transcript remains authoritative.

items.title: Room sessions never flag when the debated price has drifted from today's live price
items.why: provenance_lint.py's own check computes this drift server-side (GHNI: session price Rs 1132.31 vs today's close Rs 1305.17, 15% stale) but only prints a console WARN — nothing persists it to a state file the dashboard reads. Meanwhile renderTranscript (app.js:~2706) and the reveal-card badge (app.js:~3779) both display price_at_session as plain fact, with no comparison to the current price anywhere in the render path. A reader can be looking at a fully 'QA checked' bull/bear case built on a price that's since moved double digits, with no on-screen signal. GHNI itself compounds this: qa is null (never verified) AND the session is 15% stale — both facts already sit in state/rooms.json but neither surfaces.
items.existing_check: read renderTranscript app.js:~2706 ('...against SYM's dossier at Rs ${fmt(room.price_at_session)}...') and the reveal-card badge app.js:~3779 ('computed asof at Rs price_at_session') — both display price_at_session, neither diffs it against the live/quant close; ran `python scripts/provenance_lint.py` directly, confirms the check exists but is console-only. Distinct from the open claim-price-stale-in-room-prose item (a persona's own written price citation vs verify.json) and ratio-stale-price-basis (PE/market-cap calc timing) — this is the session's anchor price vs today's price, not covered by either.
items.resolved_note: Fixed 2026-08-23 — scripts/room_verify.py now emits a room.price_staleness issue (new psx_data.price_staleness_pct() shared helper; sev high >=30%, medium >=15%) into state/verify.json, and dashboard/app.js (ticker page) surfaces it as a QA card with the stale-pct pill and backend-authored message — no re-derivation in JS.

items.title: 11 of 44 built Desk Room sessions have never been through the Verifier — and nothing on screen says so

items.title: pageShipped shows the past (changelog.json); nothing shows what's queued (product_backlog.json)
items.why: pageShipped (app.js:6125-6136) reads changelog.json and is explicitly retrospective ('What actually changed... most recent first'). There is no forward-looking counterpart: state/product_backlog.json already holds a curated, ranked list of upcoming improvements but nothing in dashboard/app.js reads it. A read-only 'what's next' page mirroring pageShipped's structure — title + category + why only, no score/effort/existing_check (that metadata is internal scouting detail, not reader-facing) — would close the loop on the self-improvement narrative docs/OPERATIONS.md §3c already documents, for the cost of one more static-JSON page in the pattern pageShipped already validates. Pricing-independent, no live agent runs, no recurring cost.

Read pageShipped (app.js:6125-6136) in full as the direct structural precedent: same page family (a page reading one already-produced state JSON file, reader-facing subset only), different source file and time direction, so this is a new page alongside it, not a rebuild of it.

items.why: Compared qa.checked vs reaffirmed across all 48 built rooms.json entries: 21 (44%) have reaffirmed dated AFTER qa.checked — e.g. TBL built 2026-07-20, qa.checked 2026-07-20 (verdict clean), but reaffirmed 2026-07-26 rewrote the bull/bear case content 6 days later. Same pattern on UBL, OGDC, MARI, MCB, LUCK, PSO, CNERGY and 14 others. The Verifier's clean/flagged verdict was true of a version of the case that is no longer on screen, yet renderTranscript's QA turn (app.js:~2930) and the reveal-card badge (app.js:~4006) both render it as if it still applies — neither compares room.reaffirmed against room.qa.checked. The badge is the desk's core trust signal ('QA checked' = fact-checked); showing it against stale content misrepresents what was actually verified.
items.existing_check: read renderTranscript's QA turn (app.js:~2930-2931, renders qa.checked date + verdict with no reaffirmed comparison), the blocked-verdict gate (app.js:~2950, `room.qa.verdict === "blocked"`, no date logic), and the reveal-card badge (app.js:~4006, `s.qa ? qabadge ok "QA checked" : qabadge warn "Not yet verified"` — pure truthy/falsy check). items.title: Ticker page waits for 27 state/history requests before showing its first useful section
items.why: pageTicker awaits quant, universe, live, valuation, fundamentals, Room, research, explainer, verification and multiple history/optional datasets in one Promise.all. The same block includes history requests with 300000- and 600000-ms deadlines and a retry loop, so a slow optional artifact can hold up the complete first render even when the core quote and desk read are available. No timing benchmark is assumed; the request fan-out and single await are directly visible in dashboard/app.js.
items.existing_check: Read dashboard/app.js:2998-3012: pageTicker starts and awaits all 27 j(...) calls together, including history, history_deep and intraday; the core sections are rendered only after that await resolves.
items.change: Split core ticker data from optional history, research and enrichment requests so the useful read renders first and optional sections hydrate afterward.
items.user_benefit: Less waiting and fewer blank/error retries when one non-core dataset is slow or unavailable.
items.scope_dependencies: dashboard/app.js loader/render lifecycle only; preserve existing state files, explicit missing-data copy and retry boundaries.
items.build_scope: Dashboard/app.js loader/render lifecycle; split existing core and optional requests without new dependencies or state files.
items.recommended_first_stage: Render quote, valuation, fundamentals, Room and QA from a core request group; then lazy-load deep history and optional enrichment with explicit placeholders.
items.tradeoffs: Improves resilience but increases render-state complexity; constrain the first stage to a core/optional split.
items.acceptance_test: With history_deep delayed or unavailable, core ticker sections render and remain accurate; the chart shows an explicit unavailable/loading state, later hydration does not duplicate sections, and existing retry/error behavior remains bounded.
